html:
A way of painting Greek pottery in which figures are painted in a glossy black slip on the reddish clay, with details scratched through the black and added in red and white. It began at Corinth around 700 BCE.

Corinthian black-figure vases with animal friezes sold across the Mediterranean. From the early 6th century Athens took up the style and soon dominated the market, with scenes from myth, war and daily life. Great Athenian painters include Kleitias, who painted the busy François Vase, and Exekias, whose Achilles and Ajax playing a board game is one of the best known Greek vase paintings. Many of the finest pieces were found in the tombs of Etruscan buyers.

Around 530 BCE Athenian painters invented red-figure, which allowed finer detail, and black-figure slowly faded. It lived on in the prize jars of the Panathenaic Games, which kept the old style for centuries.
sum: A way of painting Greek pottery in which figures are painted in a glossy black slip on the reddish clay, with details scratched through the black and added in red and white. It began at Corinth around 700 BCE.
